rubric_items.reason: All 15 design components have at least one threat. The appointment table that links patients (T-18) and the AppointmentsPage URL input (T-16) are covered. No background jobs exist, so none are modelled, which is correct.

Most threats fit the change: the with_today parse, bound SQL parameters, the bounded id list, day-window shifts, and appointment volume once roles exist. T-12 (type drift) is a correctness issue labelled as information disclosure.

Mitigations are mostly concrete and marked as existing or new (strict boolean with 400, bound params, early return, URL-encoded numeric id). T-15 only says paging is unchanged, and some cites point to the wrong design lines.
Both real unknowns (the permission for counts after sign-in, and whether a rate limit exists) are asked as Q-01 and Q-02 with options and defaults. Assumed controls name their basis.
Readable and consistent between the front matter and the body. Threats are ordered by component, not by risk.

findings.text: C12 cites design.md#L203, but L203 describes the DoctorListRow type. countTodayByDoctor appears at L202, so the claim is not supported at its cited anchor.

findings.text: C11 cites design L201, which describes DoctorService. The with_today parse is at L200. T-7 uses C11 to support 'summary plus today_count only', which is stated at L203, not L201.

cites.quote: The type is the existing doctor summary plus today_count only (C11)
parses `with_today` (boolean, default false) next to the existing filters

findings.suggested_fix: Cite design.md#L200 and #L203 for C11, or add a separate claim for the row type shape.

findings.text: The design relies on GET /api/settings as the source of the hospital time zone for the link, but the threat model does not model it. T-14 refers only to design Q-03.

cites.quote: GET /api/settings, **existing**: assumed source of the hospital time zone for the web link (Q-03).
Call todayIn with the hospital time zone, not the browser's zone (design Q-03).

findings.suggested_fix: Add a line to T-14 or a new threat covering the settings read: the web falls back to a fixed default zone if the call fails.

findings.text: T-12 is labelled information_disclosure, but it describes type drift that causes undefined values to render. That is a correctness risk, not a disclosure threat.

cites.quote: The web type could expect fields the API does not send, so the page renders stale or undefined values.

findings.suggested_fix: Reclassify T-12 as tampering or integrity, or drop it as out of scope for STRIDE.

findings.text: Threats are listed in component order. The highest-risk items (T-20 privilege over appointment volume, T-1 no sign-in) appear last or first by chance, not by risk.

cites.quote: T-20 doctorsRouter, elevation of privilege: counts readable without appointment permission once roles exist

findings.suggested_fix: Order the Threats section by risk, or add a risk rating per threat.
